title: Innocence
subject: Father and baby
alt: Innocence — a sleeping newborn cradled in a father's hands, pastel pencil
story: A newborn asleep in a father's hands. Roosevelt drew this piece to show the quiet strength of Black fathers, a side of family life he feels the world does not see enough. Look closely at the fingers and the folds of skin: every one is built from hundreds of fine strokes of pastel pencil. It is the work that opened the door to the de Young Museum.

title: Father's Love
subject: Man holding baby
alt: Father's Love — a father asleep with his newborn against his chest, charcoal
story: A father asleep with his newborn against his chest. Drawn in black and white so nothing distracts from the hold.
short: A father asleep with his newborn against his chest. Drawn in black and white so nothing distracts from the hold.

title: Provider
subject: Mother and baby
alt: Provider — a baby carried in a woven sling, pastel pencil
story: A child carried close while the work goes on. Every bead, strand and fold of cloth is drawn by hand.

title: Sister's Love
subject: Sister carrying brother
alt: Sister's Love — a young girl carrying her little brother on her back, pastel pencil
story: A sister carrying her brother on her back under an open sky. The beads, the cloth and the two faces are each built up layer by layer.

title: Cool Breeze
subject: Landscape
alt: Cool Breeze — a wooden dock on a still river at golden hour, pastel
story: A quiet dock at the end of the day. One of the artist's landscapes.

alt: Young Man Overcoming Obstacle — a boy reading in bed by window light, charcoal
story: A boy reading in bed by the light of a window. Drawn in charcoal.
